recipes.reason: Restore stock, dumpling, broth and finishing section context lost by flattening; otherwise all ingredients could enter the stock.
ingredients: Stock: 5 lbs chicken bones, necks, and backs
Stock: 1 ½ cups Spanish onions, 1-inch diced
Finishing: 1 ½ cups celery, peeled and sliced ⅛ inch
Finishing: 1 ½ cups carrots, scrubbed and cut bite size
Finishing: 1 large garlic clove, crushed with skin on
Finishing: 2 cups cooked chicken (diced, shredded, dark, white, as you like)
steps: For the stock, wash blood and organs off all the chicken parts.
Bring the chicken parts and stock water to a simmer, skim, and add ice. Skim the fat consolidated by the ice.
Add the remaining stock ingredients, simmer for 40 minutes, then rest for 10 minutes.
Gently strain stock so as not to push impurities through the mesh.
Return to heat and cook down to 4 ½ quarts.
For the dumplings, fill a wide pot with salted water and bring to a simmer.
Combine the dumpling water, butter, and 1 tsp salt in a medium saucepan; bring to a simmer.
Add flour and cook on medium for about 5 minutes, bringing out a nutty aroma without browning.
Put dough in a mixing bowl, add mustard and remaining dumpling salt, and mix on low speed.
Add eggs one at a time, beating until incorporated. Add the dumpling chives.
Make quenelles with two spoons and cook about 7 minutes in the large pot of salted water. Rest on a cutting board.
For the broth, melt its butter on low heat.
Add the broth vegetables and salt, then cook on low heat for 30–35 minutes under a parchment lid.
Add the stock and simmer for 30 minutes. Strain out and discard the vegetables.
Whisk in roux a little at a time and simmer for 30 minutes, skimming impurities. Use enough roux to thicken to preference.
To finish, blanch the finishing celery in salted water until tender, then cool in an ice bath.
Put finishing carrots in a saucepan with honey, bay leaf, thyme, garlic, a pinch of salt, and water to just cover. Simmer until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add dumplings, cooked chicken, carrots, celery, and finishing chives to the soup.
Add vinegar ½ tbsp at a time to taste.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.
